clue.text: Setter and solver both know this intimate book

definitions.text: Setter and solver both know this intimate book

parts.words: Setter and solver both know this intimate book
parts.note: the person both setter and solver know is someone they share as an acquaintance, and that phrase is also the title of a Dickens novel

explanation.definitionFit: Dickens's last completed novel bears this title, which also names an acquaintance two people share.

clue.text: Disturbances over course in bad puns

indicators.note: the reversed piece sits inside the scrambled letters of the clue's word puns
bad puns are mangled ones, so the letters of puns are rearranged
over means turned over, so the word for course is read backwards

parts.note: a rut is a worn track or groove, a course a wheel follows

explanation.surface: A complaint that a run of terrible puns has upset things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' reverses the course word and 'in' sets it inside the jumbled puns, which 'bad' signals; 'course' looks like a racecourse but is a groove.
explanation.definitionFit: An upturn can mean an upheaval, so upturns are upsets or disturbances.

clue.text: Well! Seaweed contains one's muscle pain

parts.note: 'My!' and 'Well!' are both exclamations of surprise

indicators.note: the seaweed word holds the letter for one inside it

parts.note: an alga is a simple water plant such as seaweed
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims that a seaweed treatment holds the secret of their aching muscles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Well!' reads as an exclamation opening the sentence, and it is: it gives the opening interjection of the answer, while 'contains' puts the numeral inside the seaweed.
explanation.definitionFit: Myalgia is the medical term for aching or pain in a muscle.

clue.text: Six hundred chargers — employees who go to work on power cut?

definitions.meaning: Tennyson's poem describes the six hundred cavalrymen who rode into the valley of death in the Crimean War

definitions.text: employees who go to work on power cut?
definitions.meaning: read literally, a squad that restores the lights when the electricity fails

explanation.surface: Cavalry charging alongside a team of workers called out when the electricity goes off.
explanation.walkthrough: The Charge of the Light Brigade (1854, Crimean War) is famous from Tennyson's poem 'Into the valley of Death rode the six hundred'.
explanation.definitionFit: The cavalry unit in Tennyson's charge numbered six hundred; the second reading imagines a squad who fix lighting.

clue.text: Where one's expecting to get some helpful advice?

definitions.text: Where one's expecting to get some helpful advice?

parts.words: Where one's expecting to get some helpful advice?
parts.note: 'expecting' reads as hoping for, but means being pregnant: the place a pregnant woman goes for check-ups and guidance

explanation.definitionFit: Pregnant women ('expecting') attend such a clinic for medical care and advice before the birth.

clue.text: Misses having visited this refinery? It'll cost!

definitions.text: Misses having visited this refinery? It'll cost!

parts.words: Misses having visited this refinery? It'll cost!
parts.note: young ladies (misses) are polished here, and the fees are steep; 'refinery' means a place that makes people refined

explanation.definitionFit: A private school where young women were taught social graces, an expensive place for acquiring refinement.

clue.text: Dines at mess, as an alternative

indicators.note: a mess is a jumble, so the letters of the two clue words are muddled

explanation.surface: Eating in the officers' mess as a change from the usual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mess' looks like the military dining hall where one dines, but it is the anagram signal on DINES AT.
explanation.definitionFit: Instead means in place of something else, as a substitute or alternative.

clue.text: Small differences sister's having with experts, beginning to get accepted?

indicators.note: the first letter of the experts word is taken in by the sister word, moving inside it

parts.note: a nun is a religious sister
aces are people expert at something

explanation.surface: A nun mixing with experts finds she is only just starting to fit in.
explanation.walkthrough: NUN + ACES, then the beginning of ACES, its A, is 'accepted' into NUN: NU(A)N + CES.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuance is a subtle shade of meaning or slight distinction.

clue.text: A lovely time for vendettas? Slay, in massacre

indicators.note: a massacre makes carnage of things, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A grim joke about feuds and killings on the most romantic day, recalling the 1929 Chicago gang slaughter.
explanation.walkthrough: The St Valentine's Day Massacre (Chicago, 1929) gives the surface its sting; 'massacre' is the anagram signal on VENDETTAS SLAY IN.
explanation.definitionFit: February 14th is the day for lovers, a time of romance and cards.

clue.text: Repeatedly masses leave repellent African charm

indicators.note: the remaining letters are written down twice in a row
the letter for masses departs from the repellent word

parts.note: something grim is forbidding or repellent
M is the abbreviation for mass in physics

explanation.surface: Crowds keep walking away from an unpleasant African talisman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leave' drops M from GRIM, giving GRI, and 'Repeatedly' doubles it.
explanation.definitionFit: A gris-gris or grigri is an amulet worn in West Africa to ward off evil.

clue.text: Birth of new clubs in a spectacle

indicators.note: the card-suit letter is placed inside the phrase meaning a spectacle

parts.note: a scene can be a spectacle or public display
C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games

explanation.surface: A new golf club makes its debut in a showy event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts C inside A SCENE to give ASCENCE, after N.
explanation.definitionFit: Nascence is the state of coming into being, an origin or birth.

clue.text: What's served up from tablespoon is the egg dish

indicators.note: food served up is dished out rearranged on the plate, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something spooned out of a tablespoon turns out to be an egg dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served up' signals an anagram of TABLESPOON IS THE EGG, eighteen letters across both lights.
explanation.definitionFit: This pasta with a meat and tomato sauce is a staple main course.

clue.text: Like vegetable — or fruit, right away?

indicators.note: the letter for right goes away from the fruit word

parts.note: a pear is a fruit

explanation.surface: Asking whether something counts as a vegetable or, without its right, a fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A small round green seed from a pod, eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: Run, dammit!

definitions.meaning: '...!' or '... it!' is a mild oath, a polite stand-in for damn

explanation.definitionFit: Dash means sprint, and as an exclamation it is a genteel curse of annoyance.

clue.text: Dull fellow — or girl, left off?

indicators.note: the letter for left comes off the word for a girl

parts.note: a lass is a girl, especially in northern Britain and Scotland

explanation.surface: Asking whether the bore is a man or a girl who has left.
explanation.definitionFit: An ass is a foolish or stupid person, a dolt.

clue.text: A mother? I didn't have a mother!

parts.note: a dam is the mother of an animal, as of a horse

explanation.surface: Someone protests that they are not a mother and had none of their own.
explanation.walkthrough: In Genesis the first man was made from dust, so he alone had no mother.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical first man was created directly by God, never born of a woman.

clue.text: Devil of a top game

definitions.meaning: a spinning top shaped like an hourglass, its name from Italian diavolo, devil
the pastime of spinning and tossing such a top on a string between two sticks

explanation.definitionFit: The juggling toy's name comes from the word for devil, and playing with it is a game of skill.

clue.text: Obsessive about an upstanding pop star

parts.note: mad about something means obsessed with it
on means about, concerning

indicators.note: in a down clue, standing up means read from bottom to top

explanation.surface: Someone is obsessed with an honest, upright celebrity singer.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'upstanding' reads bottom to top, so the little word is turned; it looks like praise for the star's character.
explanation.definitionFit: The American singer known by one name was the biggest-selling female pop artist of the 1980s.

clue.text: See 12
It's hard to spot in one Tino Best over

indicators.note: over says the run of letters is turned over, read backwards
to spot something in a phrase is to find it lying inside the run of clue words

parts.note: Tino Best is a West Indies fast bowler

explanation.surface: Picking out a West Indies bowler's performance in one over at cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: Tino Best bowled for the West Indies; 'over' is a cricket term here but reverses the letters hidden 'in' ONE TINO BEST.
explanation.definitionFit: Ebonite is vulcanised rubber made very hard, used for things like bowling balls.

clue.text: Clot's caught after mobile goes off

definitions.note: possessive noun standing for an adjective meaning relating to a clot

indicators.note: after places the caught letter behind the scrambled phone word
something going off is breaking down or exploding, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: An idiot is caught out when his mobile phone rings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes off' scrambles the phone word, as a ringing mobile goes off; 'Clot's' reads as an insult (a clot is a fool in British slang) but means of a blood clot.
explanation.definitionFit: Embolic means relating to an embolus, a blood clot lodged in a vessel.

clue.text: Circular designations of pencil not well displayed

parts.note: pencils are graded H for hard and B for black (soft), so the grades read 'H and B'
ill means not well, unwell

explanation.surface: Someone notices the grade markings on a pencil are badly printed.
explanation.walkthrough: Pencil leads are marked H (hard) and B (soft), so 'designations of pencil' gives H AND B; 'displayed' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A circular is a leaflet handed out to many people, another word for a flyer.

clue.text: Firm order to live is hollow

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour
to be is to exist or live

explanation.surface: A company instruction to stay put sounds empty.
explanation.walkthrough: The OM is the Order of Merit, an honour given by the British monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A coombe is a short valley or deep hollow in a hillside, especially in southern England.

clue.text: Wild lion out alarming animal in the hills

indicators.note: wild things run out of control, so these letters are shaken into another order

explanation.surface: An escaped lion is a frightening creature to meet in the hills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild' signals an anagram of LION OUT ALARMING.
explanation.definitionFit: This great ape lives in the forested volcanic highlands of central Africa.

clue.text: Spoken from room in people's church, it's as good as one can get!

definitions.text: it's as good as one can get!

indicators.note: the spoken, from and room pieces are all placed inside the word for people

parts.note: men are people, persons in general
oral means spoken rather than written
ex is Latin for out of, from
a cell is a small room, as in a monastery or prison
CE is the abbreviation for the Church of England

explanation.surface: Words delivered from a side room in a community church are said to be the best possible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' places the spoken, from and room pieces inside the people word, and the church abbreviation follows. 'Spoken' looks like a homophone signal but is a plain synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Virtue of the highest kind, goodness of character beyond which no one can go.
